issue_context.title: quic-client fuzzer crash
issue_context.body:
Running with the code from #22592, with this file:
[crash-a194cdde40cabb7116f839e39810ec5e95597fd8.gz](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/files/13248688/crash-a194cdde40cabb7116f839e39810ec5e95597fd8.gz)

I got:
ssl/quic/quic_txp.c:294: OpenSSL internal error: Assertion failed: !h->done_implicit

review_comments: I considered doing it this way myself - but it wasn't clear to me whether it would work in all cases. The `pkt` structure only tells you about the current encryption level. Can it ever be that a PATH_RESPONSE frame has been emitted for a different encryption level in the datagram? In which case `pkt->force_pad` wouldn't be set here but we still need to use explicit len?

Different ELs are represented by different packets, so there is no issue putting an implicit-length STREAM frame in different ELs, because they are implicitly ended by the end of the packet, not the end of the datagram.
